finding: Seven properties of sensemaking per Weick 1995: identity, retrospection, enactment, social activity, ongoing process, cue extraction, plausibility over accuracy.
numbers: Seven properties. Definition (Weick, Sutcliffe, Obstfeld 2005): ongoing retrospective development of plausible images that rationalize what people are doing.
quote: an obsession with accuracy seems fruitless
limits: Secondary page. No effect sizes; the theory is stated as properties, not tested hypotheses.
agent_relevance: The properties are a checklist of what a scaffold could log (who am I, what cues, what story). No test shows they help a model.

finding: Social property: plausible stories are shared and kept, and the audience includes the speaker. Ongoing property: reality is an accomplishment from efforts to create order.
limits: Conceptual claims only.
agent_relevance: A single agent has no social audience; a second model instance or a later self could stand in as audience.

source: Wikipedia: Sensemaking (Mann Gulch and Bhopal citations)
finding: The page cites Weick 1993 Mann Gulch (Administrative Science Quarterly) as the anchor case. Bhopal is named only as a re-analysis linked to situated sensemaking in disasters. Tenerife and Navy ship are not on the page.
limits: Page has a source error in the volume number; Bhopal has no separate cite.
agent_relevance: Case-based theory: evidence is narrative re-analysis, not experiment.

finding: Mann Gulch, 5 Aug 1949: 15 smokejumpers plus one ground firefighter (Harrison) met a blow-up. 13 of 16 died; 3 survived (Dodge, Rumsey, Sallee).
numbers: Jump 4:10 pm; overrun about 5:55 pm (about 1 h 45 min); Harrison watch stopped 5:56. Fire about 3,000 acres in 10 min; 4,500 acres later; about 450 men took 5 more days. 11 died in the fire, 2 next day.
limits: Wikipedia summary of the case, not Weick's text. Death-count details can differ across sources.
agent_relevance: The core natural case: an equivocal cue (a small fire) turned deadly when the frame broke.

source: Wikipedia: Mann Gulch fire (Dodge escape fire)
finding: Dodge lit a grass fire and lay in the burned ground. His crew did not follow and ran uphill. Rumsey and Sallee escaped through a rock crevice.
numbers: Sallee was 17, youngest on the crew, died 2014 at 82. Rumsey died 1980 at 52.
limits: An order that did not fit the crew's frame was not obeyed. No test of what would have made them follow.
agent_relevance: An unfamiliar but correct instruction was rejected because it did not fit the current story. An agent may do the same with a tool result that contradicts its plan.

finding: Weick argued survival depended on a simultaneous collapse of sensemaking and structure: leadership shifted to Hellman, the order to drop tools broke identity, and Dodge's later commands lost legitimacy.
limits: Interpretation by one author from interviews and a book; not independently tested.
agent_relevance: Dropping tools meant dropping identity. Prompts that tell an agent to abandon a role or tool need an alternative identity.

finding: Timeline of Weick's work: Social Psychology of Organizing 1969 and 1979; loose coupling 1976; Mann Gulch 1993; Weick and Roberts flight decks 1993; Sensemaking in Organizations 1995; collective mindfulness 1999; Managing the Unexpected 2001; Organizing and the Process of Sensemaking 2005; Bhopal reflections 2010.
numbers: Dates only. Page says Weick was born 1936 and died 21 May 2026.
limits: Bibliography page, no results.
agent_relevance: Source list to follow backward.

finding: Cosmology episode: a challenge to assumptions that makes people doubt their ability to act. Introduced in the Mann Gulch analysis.
limits: Defined from one case; no measurement scale.
agent_relevance: Analog for an agent: a tool result that breaks the task frame. Could be an operator trigger, but no data show it helps.

finding: With Roberts and Sutcliffe: HROs show preoccupation with failure, reluctance to simplify, sensitivity to operations, commitment to resilience, deference to expertise.
limits: Taxonomy from field studies; not quantitative.
agent_relevance: Maps loosely to guardrails such as seeking disconfirmation.

finding: Basbøll and Graham alleged Weick misused a Holub poem in the Mann Gulch story; Weick disputed it.
limits: Concerns a narrative device, not the data.
agent_relevance: Shows the founding case is an authored narrative.

finding: Weick's organizing model: organizing is resolving equivocality in an enacted environment via enactment, selection and retention, with communication cycles (act, respond, adjust) and assembly rules.
numbers: Relations: more equivocality means fewer applicable rules and more cycles; more cycles reduce equivocality. Three steps per cycle.
quote: the resolving of equivocality in an enacted environment
limits: Verbal model; no fitted parameters, no test on this page.
agent_relevance: Closest thing to a formal model. It reads like a loop: if rules fail, run more clarification rounds. Could be coded as a stop rule.

finding: Assembly rules (SOPs, manuals) work best when equivocality is low; cycles are needed when it is high.
limits: Untested boundary condition.
agent_relevance: Use cheap rules for clear tasks and iterative clarification for ambiguous ones.

finding: Tenerife 27 Mar 1977: KLM 4805 began takeoff without clearance after an ambiguous 'We are now at takeoff' and tower 'OK'.
numbers: 583 killed, 61 survivors; KLM 248 aboard all died; Pan Am 396 aboard, 335 died. Visibility about 500 m then under 100 m.
limits: Page gives no Weick analysis; causes are from accident reports.
agent_relevance: Ambiguous token plus a prior plan led to action. Same risk for an agent reading an ambiguous 'OK'.

finding: Contributing factors: fog, radio interference, nonstandard phrases, captain seniority, duty-time pressure, a 35 min refuel delay.
numbers: Delay 35 min; over 45 tonnes of extra fuel.
limits: Dutch inquiry disputed the blame; multi-causal.
agent_relevance: Identity and status shaped sensemaking: the crew did not challenge the captain.

finding: Bhopal 2-3 Dec 1984: two rival accounts of the cause, water ingress during maintenance vs sabotage by an employee. Safety systems were off or failed.
numbers: At least 3,787 deaths (state); 2,259 official immediate; 558,125 injuries per a 2006 affidavit. Tank E610 held 42 tonnes MIC; about 30 tonnes escaped in 45-60 min.
limits: Investigators could not reproduce the water route; the company-commissioned report favored sabotage.
agent_relevance: Competing plausible stories for one event fit Weick's plausibility-over-accuracy point.

finding: Refrigeration shut in January 1982, alarm disconnected, scrubber on standby, gauge faulty for about a week, siren silenced quickly.
limits: Facts from a wiki summary.
agent_relevance: Many weak cues each explained away; the same pattern as ignoring small anomalies in a long agent run.

finding: Columbia 2003: the Mission Management Team compared the foam strike to past strikes and rejected a DoD imaging request; the DAT stopped asking afterward.
numbers: Foam 53-69 cm long, 686-922 km/h relative; impact at T+81.9 s; DAT concluded 26 Jan; program costs fell 21% 1991-94.
limits: Page cites CAIB, not Weick.
agent_relevance: Prior cases made the new anomaly plausible as normal.

finding: Challenger 1986: Thiokol engineers advised no launch below 53 F; management reversed after a recess; launch at 36 F air temperature.
numbers: 36 F air, 26 F forecast; coldest earlier launch 53 F; SRB 25 F left, 8 F right.
limits: Organizational reading by the Rogers Commission; Vaughan's normalization-of-deviance thesis is not on the page.
agent_relevance: Same structure: plausibility and schedule pressure won over the accurate cue.

source: arXiv 2410.12029 On Classification with LLMs in Cultural Analytics
finding: Abstract seen in an API listing only. Frames classification as sensemaking; prompt-based LLMs match supervised models on established tasks and do worse on new ones across ten tasks.
limits: Abstract only. Uses the word sensemaking loosely; not a Weick test.
agent_relevance: Weak link to the schema.

finding: LLM-generated overviews help human sensemaking in unfamiliar domains; three studies reported accurate overviews and better comprehension.
limits: Abstract only. Human sensemaking, not the model's own.
agent_relevance: LLMs as sensemaking aids for people, not as Weick-style agents.

finding: Within-subject study: users explored more topics and structured knowledge hierarchically with the tool.
limits: Abstract only.
agent_relevance: Tool support, no Weick property test.

source: arXiv 2409.17289 Steering LLM Summarization with Visual Workspaces
finding: A visual workspace before generation gave GPT-4 summaries that aligned better with ground truth in proof-of-concept experiments.
limits: Abstract only.
agent_relevance: Pre-structuring cues before generating resembles cue extraction.

finding: LLM plus knowledge-graph tool for analysts grouping documents; feedback from six professional analysts.
limits: Abstract only; small and qualitative.
agent_relevance: Applied branch, not Weick.

source: Modeling Student Sensemaking with LLMs and Knowledge-Graph-Guided Inference (id 2609.31046 as listed)
finding: Tests whether instruction-tuned LLMs can rate multidimensional student sensemaking, and whether knowledge-graph state improves their inference.
limits: Abstract only; id as reported by the API listing, not verified by opening.
agent_relevance: Rating of human sensemaking, not model sensemaking.

source: arXiv search for 'organizational sensemaking' in abstracts
finding: The arXiv search for the exact phrase organizational sensemaking returned 0 results. No LLM paper found tests Weick's seven properties directly.
numbers: 0 results on one query; a looser query gave 48 hits, all HCI or tool papers.
limits: One query on one date; OpenAlex and Semantic Scholar were rate-limited and WebSearch budget was spent, so coverage is incomplete.
agent_relevance: Gap: no measured LLM test of Weick's properties was found. Do not claim any.

source: Weick (1993) The collapse of sensemaking in organizations: the Mann Gulch disaster
finding: From memory, not opened: Weick reanalyzed Maclean's account. He argues the crew's frame failed and the order to drop tools removed identity.
numbers: Not read; use the Wikipedia lines for numbers.
limits: Not opened this session; treat as unverified.
agent_relevance: Primary source to read in a later pass.

finding: From memory, not opened: the book sets out the seven properties as a framework with many cases.
limits: Not opened; details unverified.
agent_relevance: Read in a later pass for formal statements.

source: Weick, Sutcliffe, Obstfeld (2005) Organizing and the process of sensemaking
finding: Not opened (page fetch failed). Restates sensemaking as retrospective development of plausible images; the definition was verified only on the Wikipedia page (a01).
limits: Fetch failed; unverified.
agent_relevance: Definition already captured.

source: Maitlis (2005) The social processes of organizational sensemaking
finding: From memory, not opened: a study of three UK symphony orchestras found four forms of sensemaking (guided, fragmented, restricted, minimal) depending on leader control and stakeholder animation.
numbers: Three orchestras; interview counts not recalled.
limits: Not opened; verify before use.
agent_relevance: A rare comparative test of the social property.
